title: feat(scenarios): an authoring turn's turn cap is sized by the card's tier; --author-max-turns and --ask-max-turns reach the live driver
body:
Fixes #31106
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:场景跑批器(私有包 `@objectstack/scenarios` 的 runner)构建回合的轮数上限改为按卡片 `tier` 取默认值(control 80、starter 300、delivery 600),新增 `--author-max-turns N` / `--ask-max-turns N` 两个参数覆盖它;每个回合记录它实际用的上限,记分卡 author 行显示「已用轮数/上限」,例如 `error_max_turns · 80/80 turns`。
- 为什么改:上限原来写死 80 且 CLI 不能改,实测 3 张 starter 卡的构建回合全部在 80 轮被截停(`error_max_turns`,15–24 分钟),没有一张中档卡能测完;control 卡只要 17–21 轮,维持 80 不变。
- 风险与回滚:只动不发布的跑批器包,平台运行时零改动;回滚就是 revert 本 PR。没有用真实 `claude` 跑过(成本裁决只许本地登录,本容器没有);starter 的 300 轮和 60 分钟超时大致同时触顶,构建仍可能以超时结束,两种情况都如实记为「未测量」。
- 先看:`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/driver.ts`(`DEFAULT_AUTHOR_MAX_TURNS` 表与 `author()` 按 `task.tier` 取上限)、`src/runner/cli.ts`(`makeDriver` 传参与回放拒收)、`src/runner/orchestrate.ts`(三处 author 调用带上 `tier: card.tier`)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run test/runner/units.test.ts test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts`,预期 84 个测试全绿。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

**The cap is resolved per authoring turn, by the card's tier** (`src/runner/driver.ts`).

- `DEFAULT_AUTHOR_MAX_TURNS`, a record keyed by `ScenarioTier`, = `{ control: 80, starter: 300, delivery: 600 }`, beside `DEFAULT_AUTHOR_TIMEOUT_MIN`, and `DEFAULT_ASK_MAX_TURNS = 12`.
- The driver is built once per CLI run (`makeDriver`) and knows no card, so `AuthorTask` gains a required `tier: ScenarioTier`. The live driver computes `--max-turns` as `--author-max-turns`, else `DEFAULT_AUTHOR_MAX_TURNS[task.tier]`. The tier is not part of the replay key (`stepKey` is unchanged), so existing recordings still replay.
- `orchestrate.ts` passes `tier: card.tier` on all three authoring calls: the scratch build, the scratch iterate, and the template iterate. The card asks for "build and iterate turns", so one cap covers both.
- Ask turns (questions and operations) take `--ask-max-turns`, else 12, on every tier.
- `ClaudeCodeDriverOptions.maxTurnsAuthor` / `maxTurnsAsk` are renamed `authorMaxTurns` / `askMaxTurns`, matching `authorTimeoutMs` / `askTimeoutMs` and the flags. Nothing set them (`git grep` at `a61f61a4`: only their own declarations and the two `??` reads).

**The CLI** (`src/runner/cli.ts`).

- `--author-max-turns N` and `--ask-max-turns N` take a whole number above 0, and any other value is refused with the flag and the value named. `makeDriver(spec, limits)` threads them to `ClaudeCodeDriver` the same way `--author-timeout` is threaded.
- A replay (`--driver recorded:F`) refuses all three live-driver limits, naming every one it was given. This matches the existing `--author-timeout` refusal: a replay re-reads each turn as it was recorded.
- The driver line now ends `· author max turns: control 80, starter 300, delivery 600 · ask max turns: 12`.

**The cap used is recorded.**

- On the turn: `TurnProcess.maxTurns` (`meta.process`, next to `timeoutMs`) is the `--max-turns` the CLI process was given, on authoring and ask turns alike, so a recording carries it.
- On the run record: `TurnSummary.maxTurns` (beside `numTurns`) in `cardRun`, and `scorecard.modes[].first.build.author` / `iterate.build.author` carry `numTurns` and `maxTurns`. `env.driver` (`DriverInfo`) carries `authorMaxTurns` (the per-tier table this run applies) and `askMaxTurns`.
- On the scorecard: the `Build · author` and `Iterate · author` rows show the turns taken of the cap, for example `error_max_turns · 80/80 turns · 23m 34s`. A turn killed before any result line shows `?/80 turns`. A turn recorded without a cap shows the count alone, and a turn with neither shows neither (the existing rows are byte-identical).

Unchanged, by ruling: a turn ending `error_max_turns` is still `not measured: author turn failed: error_max_turns`, and nothing runs after it.

Landing: `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/{driver,cli,orchestrate,scorecard,transcript}.ts`, `test/runner/{units,orchestrate}.test.ts` and the package README, all inside the claim's file surface. `src/schema.ts` is read (`ScenarioTier`, `SCENARIO_TIERS`), not changed.

## Tests

- `test/runner/units.test.ts`, inside the existing describe of the live driver against a stand-in `claude` script (never the real CLI). The stand-in gains an `ARGV` prompt that answers its own argument list, so the tests read the `--max-turns` value the CLI process was really started with:
  - **Tier default, no flag:** a control, starter and delivery author turn start the CLI with `--max-turns` 80, 300 and 600. An ask turn starts it with 12. Each turn's `meta.process.maxTurns` matches, and `info()` states the table. The literal table is pinned.
  - **The flags reach the CLI's argument list:** `parseArgs(['--author-max-turns', '450', '--ask-max-turns', '20'])` goes through `makeDriver('claude', …)`, the binary resolves on `PATH` like the `--author-timeout` test, and the CLI gets `--max-turns 450` on every tier and `--max-turns 20` on an ask turn. `0`, `-3`, `1.5` and `many` are each refused, naming the flag and the value. A replay refuses each flag and all three together, naming them.
  - The two replay-driver author tasks now name their tier. The required field caught both at typecheck.
- `test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts`:
  - An `error_max_turns` build author turn is not measured as before. `build.author` carries `numTurns`/`maxTurns`, the author row reads `error_max_turns · 80/80 turns · 23m 34s`, and the JSON-serialised run record carries the cap in `cardRun` and `scorecard`.
  - An iterate turn killed before any result line reads `?/80 turns`. A turn with neither a count nor a cap keeps its old row.
  - A new top-level describe checks that every authoring turn of the control card (scratch build, scratch iterate, template iterate) carries `control` to the driver. In the reference-cycle describe, the starter card `requisition_to_receipt` carries `starter` on its build and iterate turns.

Reverse verification: one mutation per behaviour, each through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. In every case the anchor went from 1 hit to 0, the blob changed, the restored blob equalled HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` was empty afterwards. The suites import `src/` by relative path, so no build sits between a mutation and its run.

| Mutation | Expected | Observed |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `driver.ts`: the author cap ignores the task's tier (`'control'`) | tier-default test red | 1 failed / 83 passed |
| `cli.ts`: `makeDriver` drops `authorMaxTurns` | flag test red | 1 failed / 83 passed |
| `orchestrate.ts`: the scratch build passes `tier: 'control'` | starter-card test red | 1 failed / 83 passed |
| `scorecard.ts`: the author row drops the turns text | both author-row tests red | 2 failed / 82 passed |
| `cli.ts`: the replay forgets `--author-max-turns` | flag test red (the replay opened the file instead) | 1 failed / 83 passed |
| `orchestrate.ts`: `summarize` drops `maxTurns` | both author-row tests red | 2 failed / 82 passed |

## Acceptance notes

- **Defaults: the card's example is kept, and the measurements support it.** From the card's three `starter` readings (80 turns in 23m 34s, 15m 05s and 14m 48s), a turn takes 11–18 s, so the 60-minute `--author-timeout` default allows about 200–325 turns. A cap of 300 makes the turn cap and the wall clock bind at about the same point. The cap stops a turn that loops, and the timeout stops a slow one. `control` stays at 80: its builds finished in 17–21 turns.
- **How the two caps relate on `delivery`:** no delivery card exists in the library at `a61f61a4` (9 cards: 6 `starter`, 3 `control`). At the starter pace, 600 turns would take about 110–180 minutes, past the 60-minute default, so under the default the clock ends a delivery turn first. The README and the constant's doc say a delivery run should raise `--author-timeout` too. The timeout itself is not tier-sized: the card does not ask for it, and the last PR on this package made it a flat constant on purpose.
- **Ask turns: 12 on every tier, as before.** Neither the card nor its thread has an ask-turn `error_max_turns` reading, so there is no measured reason for a per-tier table. It is a single constant.
- `--author-max-turns` sets one cap for every card in the run. A per-tier override was not asked for, so it is not added.
- Not measured live: no real `claude` run. The cost ruling allows only a local Claude Code login, and this container has none. The flag-to-argv path is pinned against the stand-in CLI. The epic seat's re-run of the six `starter` cards is the card's own verification.
- `test:repo` was not run locally. The one repo-level pin that reads this package, `packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts`, lists `referenceTargetOf` callers under `src/score/`. This diff adds no such call and touches no file there. CI's `Test Core` runs it.
- Changeset: none. `@objectstack/scenarios` is `private: true` and publishes nothing, so the PR carries `skip-changeset`.
